title: Global feature-based suppression without local target competition.
summary: Feature-based attention (FBA) enables the prioritization of behaviorally relevant stimulus features across the visual field by enhancing processing of attended and suppressing unattended information. While global amplification of attended features is well established, it remains unclear whether suppression of unattended features reflects a global mechanism or depends on local spatial competition with attended stimuli. Here, we tested whether suppression of unattended colors requires direct local competition with the attended color. title: FMRI-guided focal transcranial magnetic stimulation of anterior cingulate cortex reduces opioid seeking and restores connectivity.
source: PubMed · Proc Natl Acad Sci U S A
summary: Relapse remains a major challenge in opioid addiction treatment. Transcranial magnetic stimulation (TMS) has emerged as a potential therapeutic strategy for addiction, yet results had been mixed due to empirically selected stimulation targets and limited knowledge of neural circuit engagement. Here, we used a focal rat TMS platform to test whether high-density theta-burst stimulation (hdTBS) of the anterior cingulate cortex (ACC), a corticostriatal node implicated in opioid relapse by prior causal and longitudinal functional MRI studies, decreases relapse-like oxycodone seeking and associated circuit dysfunction. title: Benchmarking the Brain's Blood Vessels - Why We Need Specialized Models in Medical AI.
summary: AbstractWhile general-purpose multimodal and language models have made progress across many medical tasks, many clinically important problems require a precise understanding of anatomy, imaging physics, and disease-specific context that is not available in internet-scale public data. In this issue of NEJM AI, Yang et al. report the TopCoW challenge, a public benchmark for topology-aware circle of Willis segmentation on computed tomography (CT) and magnetic resonance (MR) angiography. title: Physiological Signals Boosted by Artificial Intelligence Save Time and Brain Function.
summary: AbstractPatients with acute neurologic injury in the neurologic intensive care unit are at high risk of secondary brain injury, yet timely detection and intervention remain limited by intermittent examination and delayed signal interpretation. This review explores emerging applications of artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning in neurocritical care, highlighting how continuous physiological data streams - such as electroencephalography, intracranial pressure, and cerebral blood flow - can be used to detect subclinical deterioration and guide early treatment. title: T2 mapping of individual fascicles of the sciatic nerve at 7 T using multi-echo spin-echo.
summary: Neuropathies can selectively affect individual fascicles within peripheral nerves, but diagnosis is limited by MRI spatial resolution and signal-to-noise ratio. This feasibility study aimed to leverage 7 T MRI to measure sub-millimetric T2 maps of sciatic nerve fascicles in healthy subjects. Accelerated multi-echo spin-echo sequences were acquired in six healthy volunteers at 7 T. Acceleration included generalised autocalibrating partially parallel acquisition (GRAPPA) and GRAPPATINI, which integrates GRAPPA with model-based accelerated relaxometry. title: A Reproducible MRI-to-FE Workflow for Generating Population-Specific and Subject-Specific Finite Element Head Models.
summary: Finite element (FE) models are widely used to study traumatic brain injury, but most are based on single-subject scans or generic atlases that may not represent specific cohorts, introducing variability in biomechanical outputs. This study presents a reproducible framework for generating a cohort-specific MRI-derived template brain and constructing a representative FE head model. A cohort-specific template was created from T1-weighted and diffusion-weighted MRI scans of collision sport athletes (n = 78). title: High-fat diet-induced MAFLD is associated with sleep architecture disruption via hippocampal neuroinflammation and bifurcated IRS-1/Akt/mTOR signaling in mice.
summary: Epidemiological associations between metabolic dysfunction-associated fatty liver disease (MAFLD) and sleep disturbances point to shared mechanisms, yet the underlying central pathways remain unexplored. We hypothesized that high-fat diet (HFD)-induced MAFLD disrupts sleep architecture via hippocampal neuroinflammation and dysregulation of the IRS-1/Akt/mTOR signaling axis. Male BALB/c mice were fed a control diet (CD) or a 60% HFD for 16 weeks to induce MAFLD. Sleep-wake architecture was assessed by 24-h EEG/EMG recordings. title: Imaging Features and Prognosis of Anti‑Sez6l2 Encephalitis: A Longitudinal Cohort Study and Literature Review.
summary: Anti-Seizure-Related 6 Homolog Like 2 (Sez6l2) encephalitis is a rare autoimmune disorder characterized by cerebellar ataxia and cognitive impairment. The 13 previously reported cases included in our systematic analysis focus on adults, leaving gaps in pediatric demographics, longitudinal multimodal imaging markers, and effective management of refractory cases. This study aimed to expand the clinical spectrum, evaluate multimodal imaging in localizing neuroinflammation/monitoring response, and assess the efficacy of combined first- and second-line immunotherapy. title: A closer look at LATE: a Case Report on a subtly evolving neurodegenerative disorder.
summary: Limbic-predominant age-related TDP-43 encephalopathy (LATE) often presents in older adults with a hippocampal-type amnestic syndrome that is clinically indistinguishable from Alzheimer's disease (AD). In the era of anti-amyloid therapies, misdiagnosis carries therapeutic consequences. Single-patient case report. The patient provided written informed consent and all data included in this paper are de-identified. title: Heterogeneous decision-making in ADHD: computational subtypes and their distinct prefrontal connectivity patterns.
summary: Children with ADHD exhibit decision-making deficits characterized by lower efficiency in evidence accumulation and a preference for smaller, sooner rewards in intertemporal choices. This study aimed to preliminarily explore computational subtypes of ADHD in children and to investigate differences in prefrontal functional connectivity between ADHD subtypes. A total of 94 children with ADHD and 63 typically developing children matched for sex, age, and IQ were included. title: Gain-of-Function Variants in PLAAT4 and Spinal Predominant Demyelinating Leukodystrophy.
summary: Leukoencephalopathies are clinically and etiologically heterogeneous disorders, and establishing a specific diagnosis remains challenging. Patients with unexplained spastic paraplegia and brain white matter hyperintensities (WMH) may be misdiagnosed as having multiple sclerosis, potentially exposing them to unnecessary immunosuppressive therapy. To define the clinical, radiological, and genetic features of spinal predominant demyelinating leukodystrophy with leg spasticity (SPDMLS). title: Subcortical Microstructural Changes Associated with Multiple Metal Exposure.
summary: Metal exposure has been associated with neurodegenerative disorders including Parkinson's disease (PD). This study examined microstructural changes in subcortical motor areas associated with chronic metal exposure. Subjects with/without a welding history (metal-exposed subjects; n = 23 and controls; n = 24) were examined. Brain microstructural differences were assessed by MRI diffusion metrics [mean (MD), axial (AD), radial diffusivity (RD) and fractional anisotropy (FA)] in subcortical motor areas [nigro-basal ganglia-thalamic circuit: substantia nigra (SN), caudate nucleus (CN), putamen, globus pallidus (GP), and thalamus; dentatorubral circuit: dentate nucleus (DN) and red nucleus (RN)].

title: Brain Gadolinium Biodistribution, Clearance, and Retention Following High-Dose Contrast-Agent Exposure in Mice: A Multimodal Study.
summary: We evaluated gadolinium biodistribution, clearance, and long-term brain retention following high-dose gadolinium-based contrast agent (GBCA) exposure in 90 mice. Macrocyclic and linear agents were assessed using particle-induced X-ray emission (PIXE) alongside complementary elemental, imaging, and histological methods. Following intravenous administration, gadolinium was detected in blood and multiple tissues during the acute phase, with declining blood levels and detectable urinary excretion. title: Assessment of the Efficacy and Safety of CyberKnife Radiosurgery on Optic Nerve Sheath Meningiomas.
summary: The purpose of this study was to evaluate the efficacy and safety of CyberKnife (CK) radiosurgery in patients with optic nerve sheath meningiomas (ONSM). We retrospectively identified patients with ONSM treated with CK between January 2020 and January 2024 from the Database of Chinese Neuro-Ophthalmic Diseases. CK was delivered at 23-25 Gy in 5 fractions. Best-corrected visual acuity (BCVA) and visual field mean deviation (VF MD) were assessed before treatment and at the final follow-up, with a median visual follow-up of 36 months (range, 26-64 months). title: Association of Diagnosis Age with Clinical Characteristics and MRI Findings in Multiple Sclerosis.
summary: Age at multiple sclerosis (MS) diagnosis may be associated with clinical course, inflammatory activity, and disability accrual, but evidence across the full age spectrum remains limited. We compared clinical and radiological features, phenotype distribution, and time to first post-diagnosis relapse across early-onset MS (EOMS), adult-onset MS (AOMS), and late-onset MS (LOMS). This observational study included patients with MS treated at two tertiary centers in Isfahan, Iran, combining a retrospective review of clinical records with a cross-sectional assessment at the most recent study visit. title: Neurocognitive Indices of Long COVID: Dysregulated Engagement of Inhibitory Control and Oscillatory Slowing.
summary: Persistent neurocognitive symptoms, such as "brain fog", insomnia, or fatigue, are prevalent in PASC (post-acute sequelae of COVID-19, "Long COVID"), even after mild acute illness. However, evidence for the neural underpinnings of cognitive dysregulation and altered spontaneous neural activity is inadequate. EEG data were acquired during an inhibitory Go/NoGo task and wakeful rest from young, otherwise healthy adults with PASC approximately six months after recovery from mild COVID-19. title: Clinical Phenotypes, Neuroimaging, and Outcomes in Prolonged and Persistent Non-Motor Migraine Aura: A Systematic Review and Episode-Level Synthesis.
summary: Prolonged and persistent migraine aura may mimic cerebral ischemia, but its clinical course and neuroimaging features are poorly characterized. We synthesized episode-level evidence on non-motor aura lasting more than 60 min without reported established infarction. This systematic review (International Prospective Register of Systematic Reviews [PROSPERO] CRD420261461238) followed the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) 2020 guidelines. title: Early Diagnostic Classification of Alzheimer's Disease Using Structural and Resting-State Functional MRI.
summary: Background: Alzheimer's disease (AD) is an irreversible neurodegenerative disorder where early diagnosis at the mild cognitive impairment (MCI) stage is critical for timely intervention. While structural MRI (sMRI) and resting-state functional MRI (rs-fMRI) provide complementary pathological information, clinical translation is limited by high feature heterogeneity and the heavy computational burden of 3D deep learning networks. This study aims to propose a lightweight, hybrid multimodal fusion model to overcome these limitations and improve diagnostic efficiency. title: When Flow Voids Are Missed: Delayed Diagnosis of Foix-Alajouanine Syndrome-A Case Report.
summary: Introduction: Foix-Alajouanine syndrome (FAS) is a rare, progressive congestive ischaemic myelopathy caused by a spinal dural arteriovenous fistula (SDAVF). Because of its non-specific clinical presentation and subtle imaging features, FAS is frequently misdiagnosed; in particular, perimedullary flow voids-its characteristic imaging hallmark-are readily overlooked on initial MRI, leading to diagnostic delay and potentially harmful interventions. title: Cryptococcal Meningoencephalitis with Possible Clinical-Manometric Intracranial Pressure Dissociation in a Pediatric Patient.
summary: A 12-year-old previously healthy girl without an identified immunodeficiency presented with a 25-day history of headache, vomiting, and severe asthenia. Cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) analysis confirmed Cryptococcus gattii meningoencephalitis. Despite consistently normal intracranial pressure (ICP) readings on serial lumbar punctures (all below 20 cm H2O), the patient developed clinical signs suggestive of raised intracranial pressure, progressing to decreased consciousness requiring ICU admission and orotracheal intubation. title: The Prevalence of Neurological Symptoms in the Presence of Plantar Fasciitis: A Review of 459 Patients.
source: PubMed · J Am Podiatr Med Assoc
summary: Background: To determine the overall incidence of concomitant neurological symptoms and, if present, their origin. Methods: A clinical review was conducted of 459 patients from a large Podiatric Medical practice, who presented with a diagnosis of plantar fasciitis. Results: A diagnosis of plantar fasciitis presented clinical neurological findings in 49% (225 of 459) of study patients. With conservative treatment, neurological symptoms resolved in 126 of 225 patients (56%), leaving 99 nonresponding patients having persistent neurological symptoms. title: Color and Spatial Cue Modulation of Emotional Word Processing: Evidence from ERPs.
summary: Emotional word processing is shaped by lexical meaning and concurrent perceptual context. This study investigated when red and green color cues and symbolic upward and downward direction cues modulate the processing of positive and negative Chinese emotional words. Thirty-four native Chinese speakers were recruited, and 27 remained in the final ERP sample after behavioral and EEG-quality exclusions. The experiment used a 2 (color: red vs. green) × 2 (direction: up vs. down) × 2 (word valence: positive vs. negative) within-subject design. title: Preschool Outcome After Therapeutic Hypothermia in Neonatal Hypoxic-Ischemic Encephalopathy: Insights from Early Neurodevelopmental Assessment.
summary: Background: Therapeutic hypothermia has significantly improved the prognosis of infants with hypoxic-ischemic encephalopathy (HIE), shifting the focus of follow-up toward the identification of early predictors of preschool neurodevelopmental outcome. This study aimed to evaluate the predictive value of early neurological, developmental and neuroradiological assessments in children with HIE treated with therapeutic hypothermia. Methods: We conducted a prospective longitudinal study including 105 children with HIE treated with therapeutic hypothermia between 2015 and 2022 at a tertiary neonatal center. title: Neurophysiological and Psychophysical Biomarkers for Predicting Spinal Cord Stimulation Treatment Response in Chronic Neuropathic Pain: A Systematic Review.
summary: Background: Spinal cord stimulation (SCS) is an established therapy for chronic neuropathic pain, yet a substantial minority of implanted patients do not obtain durable relief, and patient selection still relies largely on a subjective percutaneous stimulation trial. Objective neurophysiological and psychophysical biomarkers could enable precision selection, but their predictive value has not been consolidated across modalities. title: ImageNet, RadiologyNET, or RadImageNet? Evaluating Pretraining Across CT, MRI, and X-Ray Classification.
summary: Due to the limited availability of annotated medical datasets, medical image classification typically relies on transfer learning from large-scale natural image datasets such as ImageNet. However, it remains unclear when domain-specific pretraining offers greater benefits. This study evaluates the impact of different pretrained weights on neural network performance in radiological image classification tasks. Four strategies were compared: ImageNet, RadiologyNET, and RadImageNet model fine-tuning against learning from randomly initialised weights (Baseline). title: Blood Cell Imaging Analysis for Multiple Sclerosis Classification Using Leave-One-Subject-Out Study with Deep Neural Networks.
summary: Multiple sclerosis (MS) is a chronic neurological disease whose diagnosis typically relies on resource-intensive and partly invasive procedures such as MRI and spinal fluid analysis. This study explores whether deep learning can identify distinguishing patterns in RBC images associated with MS, aiming to determine whether blood-cell imaging may provide information relevant to understanding the disease. title: Variational Autoencoders for Medical Image Segmentation: A Review.
summary: Medical image segmentation plays an important role in healthcare because it transforms raw scans into useful information for diagnosis and treatment planning. Despite the strong performance of deep learning, most supervised segmentation methods require large amounts of pixel-level annotations and may become less reliable when imaging modalities are incomplete or when prediction uncertainty is not properly considered. title: A GPU-Accelerated MRI Simulator for Synthetic Image Generation.
summary: Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI) is an imaging technique that provides detailed structural and functional information about organs and tissues. To support the validation of MRI measurement techniques and provide a tool for scanner benchmarking, we develop an MRI simulator exploiting graphics processing units (GPUs) for computational acceleration. The GPU-Accelerated MRI Simulator (GAMS) enables us to generate synthetic images with high-resolution detail for quantitative estimation of relaxation times. title: A Mild Neurodevelopmental Phenotype Associated with a Novel BRAT1 Variant: Expanding Genotype-Phenotype Correlations.
summary: Background:BRAT1-related disorders constitute a continuous neurodevelopmental spectrum ranging from rigidity and multifocal seizure syndrome, lethal neonatal form (RMFSL) to milder phenotypes characterized by cerebellar involvement and variable developmental impairment. Genotype-phenotype correlations remain incompletely defined, particularly for missense variants that may retain residual function. Objectives: To characterize clinical and molecular findings in a patient with a mild BRAT1-related phenotype. title: A Complementary Dual-Branch Receptive Field Network for Cross-Channel-Density Motor Imagery EEG Decoding.
summary: Brain-computer interfaces (BCIs) enable direct communication between the brain and external devices, providing a bio-inspired link between humans and artificial systems. However, electroencephalography (EEG)-based motor imagery (MI) decoding continues to pose challenges, due to limited temporal exploitation and insufficient spatio-temporal modeling. To alleviate these limitations, a complementary dual-branch receptive field network (DBRFNet) is proposed for cross-channel-density MI-EEG decoding. title: MRI-Based Radiomics Model for Pretreatment Prediction of Pathological Lymph Node Metastasis in Neuroendocrine Carcinoma of the Cervix: Dual-Center Development and External Validation.
summary: Objectives: To develop and externally validate MRI-based radiomics and clinicoradiomics models for predicting pathological lymph node metastasis (LNM) in neuroendocrine carcinoma of the cervix (NECC). Methods: This retrospective two-center study included 133 patients who underwent pretreatment pelvic MRI and pathological nodal assessment: 93 for development and 40 for external validation. title: Secondary Intracranial Hypertension During ATRA/ATO Therapy in High-Risk Acute Promyelocytic Leukemia: A Case Report and Practical Management Framework.
summary: All-trans retinoic acid (ATRA) combined with arsenic trioxide (ATO) is the standard of care for acute promyelocytic leukemia (APL), including high-risk disease. Secondary intracranial hypertension (SIH), historically termed pseudotumor cerebri (PTC), is a recognized but uncommon and potentially therapy-limiting complication of retinoid exposure, reported predominantly in pediatric and young-adult patients and most frequently during induction. title: Label-Free Acoustic Wave Detection of Myelin Basic Protein for Monitoring of Neurodegenerative Disease.
summary: Myelin basic protein (MBP) is released into cerebrospinal fluid during demyelination and is therefore a promising biomarker for the detection of neurodegenerative diseases such as multiple sclerosis. For the label-free detection of MBP, we developed an antifouling aptasensor based on thickness shear mode sensing. title: Melanin Bias in Cerebral fNIRS: A Monte Carlo Study Toward Equitable Optical Brain Sensing.
summary: Functional near-infrared spectroscopy (fNIRS) is an optical biosensing modality that transduces cortical hemodynamics into a measurable near-infrared signal, underpinning wearable brain monitors and brain-computer interfaces (BCIs). Because epidermal melanin is a strong near-infrared absorber, device sensitivity may depend on skin tone, raising an equity concern for optical neural biosensors. title: From Global Evidence to Saudi Practice: A Structured Evidence Map of the Diagnosis, Molecular Targets, and Therapeutic Strategies of Multiple Sclerosis in the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia.
summary: Multiple sclerosis (MS) has shifted in a generation from an uncommon diagnosis in Saudi Arabia to a major cause of neurological disability in young adults. Available Saudi data describe clinical characteristics broadly similar to those reported elsewhere in the Middle East and do not show that Saudi patients differ from trial populations, although this does not establish equivalent efficacy or safety. title: Conductive Polyvinyl Alcohol-Based Hydrogels for Wearable Electronics: Preparation Strategies, Conductivity Enhancement, and Sensing Applications.
summary: Conductive poly(vinyl alcohol) (PVA)-based hydrogels combine electrical functionality with the mechanical compliance and biocompatibility required for wearable bioelectronics. title: Perinatal Brain Injuries in Preterm Infants.
summary: Preterm infants are vulnerable to brain injury because of immature white matter, vascular regulation, and neuroprotective mechanisms. title: Altered Neural Pitch Encoding in Vestibular Schwannoma: Evidence From Frequency-Following Responses.
source: PubMed · J Otolaryngol Head Neck Surg
summary: Vestibular schwannomas (VSs) frequently cause hearing dysfunction, yet standard clinical assessments may not fully capture neural processing deficits. title: The impact of depressive symptoms on supraspinal pain neuromodulatory functional connectivity and therapeutic implication.
summary: Background: Both depressive and pain symptoms are highly prevalent and relevant comorbid conditions in Veterans with Gulf War Illness (GWI). title: Dissociable anterior and posterior beta-burst dynamics track thought disorder in schizophrenia.
summary: Thought disorder in schizophrenia likely reflects disrupted maintenance of internal models during predictive processing. title: Assessment of Glucose Metabolism in Vivo in the Human Frontal Lobe Using Interleaved 1H and 13C MRS at 7T.
summary: 13C magnetic resonance spectroscopy (MRS), combined with 13C-labeled substrate infusion, offers a nonionizing, minimally invasive method for assessing fluxes through the main cerebral energy metabolism pathways. title: Perivascular Diffusivity and Periventricular Susceptibility Changes in Relapsing-Remitting Multiple Sclerosis: A Combined DTI-ALPS and QSM Study.
summary: Progressive periventricular damage in multiple sclerosis (MS) has been linked to impaired perivascular clearance and to susceptibility changes attributed to iron deposition and myelin loss. summary: To evaluate the effects of cerebellar continuous theta burst stimulation (cTBS) in insomnia disorder (ID). title: Sudden Onset Occipital Headache as a Presenting Feature of Ischaemic Stroke.
summary: Headache is an uncommon presenting feature of ischaemic stroke, and when it occurs, it is usually moderate and sustained rather than sudden and self-limiting. title: Assessment of Early Detection Practices for Infants at Risk of Cerebral Palsy in Lebanon: A Cross-Sectional Survey of Multidisciplinary Clinicians.
summary: Evidence-based guidelines, published in 2017, recommend confirming a diagnosis of Cerebral Palsy (CP) before 6 months of corrected age. title: Acute Transverse Myelitis Complicating the Third Trimester of Pregnancy: A Rare Case of Progressive Neurological Recovery and Favorable Obstetric Outcome.
summary: Transverse myelitis (TM) is a rare immune-mediated inflammatory disorder of the spinal cord. It can result in sensory, motor, and autonomic deficits of varying severity. title: Effects of dance and music training on the plasticity of the core empathy network: intra- and inter-network connectivity.
summary: Dance and music are two of the oldest and most universal forms of artistic expression, each requiring extensive training. title: Recurrent belly dancer dyskinesia in pregnancy with postpartum resolution.
summary: Belly dancer dyskinesia (BDD) is a rare movement disorder characterized by involuntary, repetitive contractions of the abdominal wall. Pregnancy-associated BDD is exceptionally uncommon, and recurrence in subsequent pregnancies has rarely been reported. We describe the case of a 29-year-old woman in her first pregnancy who developed involuntary abdominal movements at 16 weeks. Her medical history included hypertension and multiple uterine fibroids. Neurological assessment, laboratory investigations, and spinal magnetic resonance imaging were unremarkable, and a clinical diagnosis of BDD was established. title: The b-Value Dependence for Higher-Degree Spherical Harmonic Powers of the Diffusion MRI Signal Follows Stick Model Predictions in White Matter.
summary: To compare the dependence on b-value of the spherical harmonic powers for the diffusion MRI signal in white matter to theoretical predictions from the stick model of water diffusion within axons. Diffusion MRI data were acquired at 3 T in three healthy adults with 10 b-value shells (b = 1000-10 000 s/mm2) and 64 directions per shell. title: Assessment of fine motor performance and motor speed in pediatric patients with juvenile myoclonic epilepsy.
summary: In this study, we evaluated the fine motor functions of children and adolescents diagnosed with juvenile myoclonic epilepsy (JME) and compared them with those of a healthy control group. title: Substantia nigra iron-related alterations, white matter disruption, and functional network dysconnectivity in temporal lobe epilepsy: a multimodal neuroimaging study.
summary: Although the substantia nigra (SN) has been implicated in temporal lobe epilepsy (TLE) pathophysiology, clinical studies remain scarce. This study included 20 right-TLE (RTLE), 21 left-TLE (LTLE), and 23 healthy controls (HCs). title: Dysglycemia during neonatal encephalopathy and early school-age neurodevelopmental outcomes.
summary: To assess the relationship between neonatal dysglycemia and early school-age neurodevelopmental outcomes after neonatal encephalopathy. title: Association of CT-Derived Skeletal Muscle Radiodensity and Index With Cerebral Small Vessel Disease: A Community-Based Study.
summary: Skeletal muscle composition is linked to metabolic health, but its association with cerebral small vessel disease (CSVD) remains unclear. title: Foraminal subependymal nodules and subependymal giant cell astrocytoma in children with tuberous sclerosis.
summary: To characterize the growth patterns of foraminal subependymal nodules (fSENs) in children with tuberous sclerosis complex (TSC), and identify high-risk periods and predictors of subependymal giant cell astrocytoma (SEGA) development. title: Cortical Motor Hierarchy Disruption Is Associated With Functional Status in Early Amyotrophic Lateral Sclerosis.
summary: Amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS) is a devastating neuromuscular disease characterised by progressive muscle wasting and functional decline. title: [Posterior periventricular white matter lesions as a clue to the diagnosis of folate deficiency with compound heterozygous MTHFR polymorphisms: a case report].
summary: An 18-year-old woman presented with a one-month history of persistent dizziness. title: [Eltrombopag-associated bilateral internal jugular vein thrombosis presenting with visual impairment and marked intracranial hypertension: a case report].
summary: We report an 86-year-old man with immune thrombocytopenia (ITP) who developed bilateral internal jugular vein (IJV) thrombosis during treatment with eltrombopag (EPAG). He had experienced multiple cerebral infarctions over several months, but their cause had remained undetermined and warfarin therapy had been continued. title: Treadmill or Overground? Cognitive-Motor Interference Effects in Healthy Older Individuals.
summary: Walking is increasingly understood as a cognitively demanding activity requiring the integration of sensory processing, motor control and executive functions. title: Sequence-dependent differences in cervical nerve root visualization on magnetic resonance imaging in dogs.
summary: Cervical nerve roots transmit motor and sensory information and are often affected by neurologic disorders. title: Epipharyngeal sensory stimulation is associated with changes in brainstem-cortical functional connectivity and circulating proteomic profiles.
summary: Neurostimulation has emerged as a potential approach for modulating autonomic and neuroimmune function. Because epipharyngeal mucosa receives sensory innervation from cranial afferents, mechanical stimulation of this region may engage neural pathways. Epipharyngeal abrasive therapy (EAT) involves mechanical and chemical stimulation of the epipharyngeal mucosa and is used clinically for chronic epipharyngitis; however, its central and systemic effects remain poorly understood. title: Global synchrony moderates sad mood and is associated with emotional Stroop interference and somatic symptoms.
summary: Mood-congruent attention in depression has been studied via emotional interference tasks, including tasks comparing responses to sad and happy stimuli. Mood induction offers a way to experimentally induce sad mood in non-clinical samples and examine its association with subsequent emotional interference, including Sad-Happy interference. Previous studies have separately linked resting-state global neural dynamics (synchrony, metastability) to depressive symptoms and attentional processing. title: Puberty, not age, marks the start of adolescent brain structural remodeling.
summary: Many studies have shown that pubertal changes are associated with brain changes, but there lacks a clear understanding of what happens to the brain at puberty, and whether it opens the brain structural remodeling that characterizes adolescence. In this study, we used three longitudinal waves of structural MRI data from thousands of participants of the ABCD study aged 9-14 years to compare brain changes between age-matched children who had either reached or not reached a major pubertal milestone: menarche in females and fonarche (voice drop) in males. We found that only the children who had reached the milestone exhibited widespread contraction of cortical surface area and subcortical volume.

title: Clinical feature-guided targeted genetic testing in early-onset developmental and epileptic encephalopathy: a real-world diagnostic approach in a resource-limited setting.
summary: In low- and middle-income countries (LMICs), access to trio-based whole-exome or whole-genome sequencing is limited, which may delay genetic diagnosis in developmental and epileptic encephalopathies (DEE). We used clinical features to guide targeted genetic testing and reviewed the results through multidisciplinary discussion in a Vietnamese pediatric cohort with early-onset DEE and examined its association with treatment decision-making. summary: To compare the differences in functional brain activity between patients with temporal lobe epilepsy comorbid with depressive disorder (TLE-D) and those with temporal lobe epilepsy without depressive disorder (TLE-ND) via a meta‑analysis of resting‑state functional magnetic resonance imaging (rs-fMRI) studies, and to explore the functional brain activity features associated with depressive symptoms. title: Delayed cerebral myelination in a patient with isodicentric chromosome 18 [psu idic(18)(q21.2)] mosaicism: a case report.
summary: Isodicentric chromosome 18 is a rare structural chromosomal abnormality, with few reported cases. title: Revealing contour integration-related ERPs through temporal separation from early visual evoked potentials.
summary: Contour integration has been proposed to involve coordinated processing across hierarchical cortical regions. title: U-NeXt: General-purpose event detection for neonatal EEG
summary: We developed U-NeXt, a general framework for neonatal electroencephalography (EEG) event detection based on semantic segmentation. Its convolutional encoder-decoder directly segments individual channels using long input segments to preserve temporal context. A shared architecture and training framework were developed using low-voltage interval, artefact, and seizure datasets containing 51, 98, and 278 neonates, respectively, comprising over 11,000 hours of EEG and 82,000 annotated events. title: Interpreting Supervised Pairwise Graph Representations: Local Evidence, Confounding, and Provable Post-hoc Correction
summary: Supervised pairwise graph representations convert pairwise predictive relations into sample-specific graphs, but graph-level accuracy does not by itself show that higher-order topology carries the signal. title: Phase-based Edge Coupling: Modeling Overlapping Functional Architectures and High-Order Edge-to-Edge Interactions in EEG Networks
summary: Network neuroscience has traditionally relied on node-centric approaches, which are inherently limited in capturing the brain's overlapping functional architectures and higher-order edge-to-edge interactions. title: CFBrainAug: Modularity-Induced Counterfactual Brain Network Augmentation for Interpretable fMRI-based Autism Diagnosis
summary: Machine learning on resting-state functional magnetic resonance imaging (rs-fMRI) brain networks is promising for diagnosing Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD), but existing methods are prone to overfitting on limited training data, and their post-hoc statistical attribution offers limited clinical interpretability. title: Controlled Evaluation of EEG Foundation Models: Random Initialisation, Band-Power and Validation-Selected Probes
summary: EEG foundation models report downstream gains, yet their protocols seldom include three controls.
